hero.sub: Thirteen years turning ideas into fast, considered web products, from partner platforms at Dailymotion to design-driven front-ends. In love with JavaScript.

body: I build across the whole stack, but I care most about the layer people actually feel: the interface. Motion, typography, timing, the small things that make a product feel alive.

I've shipped for Dailymotion, the Renault Group, Roole and Arval: React and GraphQL on the front, Node, .NET and PHP behind it, Docker to hold it together. Off the clock you'll find me on CodePen and CSS Battle, or making music.

lab.intro: Side projects I build and ship on my own time: an iOS app, tools, games and code tricks. Grab what's useful.

items.title: Simply Weather
items.teaser: A no-nonsense iOS weather app, on the App Store. Current sky, next hours, done.
items.linkLabel: Get it on the App Store
items.desc: A weather app that answers the only question that matters: what is the sky about to do? Built with web tech and shipped native through Capacitor, with geolocation, haptics and local notifications, and distributed on the App Store. Designed to open fast, read at a glance and stay out of your way.

items.title: Freelance Radar
items.teaser: A personal radar for freelance dev missions: scans ~27 sources, filters, scores and tracks them.
items.desc: Hunting freelance work means fifteen tabs of stale, duplicated listings. Freelance Radar flips it: one click scans ~27 sources (LinkedIn posts, Free-Work, Codeur, remote boards…), keeps only real dev missions matching your profile and daily rate, scores them with AI, then helps you close with offer analysis, tailored outreach and kanban follow-ups. Everything runs locally: your keys, cookies and data never leave your machine.

items.title: Snake CS2D
items.teaser: Snake × Counter-Strike: plant the bomb, defuse it, don't touch anybody.
items.desc: What happens when you mix Snake with Counter-Strike? A multiplayer browser game: two teams of snakes, T side grabs the bomb and plants it on site, CT defuses, 45-second rounds, first to 13 wins. Snake rules still apply: touch a body and you are gone. Works on mobile with on-screen controls.

items.title: Motion & layout pens
items.teaser: Reusable CSS tricks: fluid type scales, scroll-driven reveals, container-query patterns.
items.desc: A growing collection of reusable CSS tricks I keep coming back to: fluid type scales, scroll-driven reveals, container-query components and the little motion details that make an interface feel alive. Every pen is copy-paste ready.
